title: Lesson 02 in the frozen grammar: moments as claims
description: Express lesson 02 (bring-up) in lesson 01's grammar as the first test of it. Claims (from today's outcomes, unchanged in substance): (1) The CLI and Bicep create Azure and seed the cluster; Flux assembles the workloads; controllers keep them healthy: moment Create Azure to Assemble OSDU, focus workstation, aks, bootstrap, flux, evidence flux. (2) A successful spi up exit is the first of five milestones, not readiness; spi status --watch follows the rest: moment Use the stack, focus readiness, initialization, caller, evidence readiness. (3) spi down removes compute and data but keeps identities and the resource group: moment Remove the stack, focus retained, evidence retained. Each claim gets a headline under twelve words, its full sentence, a why, focus, scopes, evidence, crossing. Selecting a claim selects its moment; the six moments stay the sequence control. The per-moment auto-open detail becomes a Look closer line. Candidate headline: One command creates the environment. Flux finishes it. Litmus: after it, can you explain how the stack gets created, with the drawer closed.
acceptance_criteria: Claims render with headlines; selecting a claim moves the moment and focuses the map; drawer closed by default; easy mistake then What you can now say then Next; npm run check green; second-agent review before push to main.
notes: SCOPE: src/content/chapters.js (bring-up entry), src/components/pages.js, src/main.js, src/styles/pages.css, tests/content.test.js, docs/. Branch feat/lesson-02-claims. Lesson 02 has six creation moments as steps (src/content/creation-moments.js); claims map onto moments, so selecting a claim navigates to its moment's step and the moment's own change is the focus. Keep the moment controls; they are the lesson's sequence. Drop the per-moment default detail auto-open (the drawer stays closed until asked) and replace it with a Look closer line under the moment story that opens the drawer. VERIFY: npm run check (format, 13+ tests, build); npx vite --port <own port> --strictPort and screenshot the lesson at 1440 and 390 with headless Chrome (/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome --headless=new --screenshot=<file> --window-size=1440,1100 <url>); probe the DOM for: drawer closed on load, selecting each claim changes the focused components, litmus answerable from page text with the drawer closed. CONTEXT: read AGENTS.md (interaction hierarchy and the lesson grammar), CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/iteration-6.md, then src/content/chapters.js (running-stack is the reference lesson: goal, outcomes as claims with headline/text/why/focus/scopes/evidence/crossing, example.scopes and example.crossing), src/components/pages.js (hasClaims, claimStrip, chapterOutcomes, example strip), src/main.js (lessonState, applyPolicy, expandInspector), tests/content.test.js (claims test). FORBIDDEN: never push or merge to main from the worktree (commit on your branch only); never hand-write commit messages, use git commit -m "$(aipr commit -s)"; no Claude or AI attribution anywhere; never rename or drop a route key, chapter key, or detail id; do not edit dist/, src/content/transcripts/, docs/reference/; do not touch the review preview on port 8875 or the dev port 5173; do not add PR-point-in-time comments in source. REPORT: branch name and commits, what the lesson now looks like (screenshot paths), the litmus answer as read from page text with the drawer closed, npm run check output tail, anything left undone.

title: Round 4 tunes: short claim headlines, quiet rail, drawer content rule
description: Reviewer round 4 (13 Sep 2026): claim headlines were paragraph-like; inactive rail lessons carried subtitles; the drawer invariant needed to be a review rule. Done on main in 4b7ed98: claims gain a headline field rendered as the control label with the reason underneath (the full sentence still feeds What you can now say); rail subtitles show only on the current lesson; AGENTS.md carries the lesson grammar, the two-to-four claim range, and the rule that nothing required for What you can now say lives only in the drawer. Tests assert headline length and claim count.

title: Interaction hierarchy for Learn: claim is primary, everything else is evidence
description: Decided 13 September 2026 from the reviewer's third round. In a lesson: the claim is the primary interaction and changes the map; 'How we know' opens the drawer on the best evidence item; hops are subordinate and collapsed until asked; only the evidence component advertises Inspect in Lesson focus; receded components stay clickable with the affordance on hover; boundaries never recede. Local toggle is 'Lesson focus | Explore map' to avoid two levels of the word Explore. Deep links with ?detail= open the drawer. The drawer is a contextual evidence drawer, not a sidebar: it appears because the learner asked and then goes away. Headlines are the sentence to remember; the lesson name lives in the rail and position line. 'Listen to this lesson' waits for a per-lesson narration recorded from the claims; until then the cue row is labelled 'Hear it explained' in the optional band.
notes: Round 4 (13 Sep 2026) added: the lesson grammar is frozen as the standard (see AGENTS.md); claims carry a short headline as the control and the full sentence as the carry-forward line; two to four claims per lesson, count set by content; the review rule is that nothing required for What you can now say lives only in the drawer, and details answering how to prove, check, or debug belong in the drawer; navigation stays as is (LEARN rail plus Explore · Listen · Field guides); the book labels stay as quiet labels; the Easy mistake to What you can now say sequence is standard in every lesson.

title: Pilot lesson 01 with 4–5 engineers who know OSDU and not Azure SPI
description: Three questions, watched, no scores: (1) Without clicking anything, what are the three things this lesson is trying to teach you? (2) After using the claims, can you explain what the map is showing without opening the inspector? (3) When you click How we know, does the drawer feel like useful evidence or like you left the lesson? Record where they stop and which labels they misread. Decide from the answers whether to propagate the shape (epic D) or adjust it first.
acceptance_criteria: Notes filed as a dated doc in docs/; go/no-go recorded on the roll-out epic.
notes: Revised 13 Sep: the pilot runs alongside the roll-out and no longer gates 04 to 06; findings land as beads. Daniel reviewed 01 to 03 and the round-five reviewer confirmed the structure.

title: Roll the lesson shape to 02–06 and unify the evidence component
description: Reviewer round 4 (13 Sep 2026) froze lesson 01's grammar: position line, headline, question and goal, two to four claims, one claim-focused map, optional evidence in the drawer, one easy mistake, What you can now say, next-lesson bridge, optional band. Lessons 02 and 03 are the test of that grammar and no longer wait for the pilot; 04, 05, 06 follow once 02 and 03 express cleanly and the pilot has run. Per lesson: outcomes become claims with headline, text, why, focus, scopes, evidence, crossing (02 and 05 keyed by moment; 05 already has active lanes). 03 gains the cache-down trace variant (same five hops, fourth throws, fifth answers). 05 gains a one-line bridge saying how the provider fix reached main (told in 04's hops today). 06 keeps the state panel on the map and repeated at the top of the drawer, and gets its own litmus question distinct from 05. One evidence component renders the drawer, the easy mistake, the 21 cards on 07, and the marker source-check notes. Optional 'here' override per chapter for details shared between scenes (client, image). Claim count follows the content, not lesson 01's three.
acceptance_criteria: Each lesson answers its litmus question from the page with the drawer closed; every claim has a headline under twelve words; the Easy mistake to What you can now say sequence is present; npm run check green; a second agent reviews before push.
notes: Revised 13 Sep: lessons 04 to 06 no longer wait for the pilot. They follow the seven round-five fixes (fn-kbc, fn-loo, fn-0wv covering fn-mjx/fn-5pw/fn-wes, fn-p2j, fn-e7u) and the Try it band renderer (fn-u9u), and each is written with its Try it band from the start (design artifact revision 6, section 5).

comments.author: Daniel Scholl
comments.text: Revision 6 review: Lesson 06 needs a tested descriptor/workflow combination and an eligible change that builds and publishes an image, in addition to onboarding. A descriptor-only or Markdown-only change does not establish that path; a green Validation Summary may mean deployment was skipped. The demonstrated outcome should include the deploy-test gate entering, expected digest reaching a ready pod, at least one non-skipped test with no failures, and restoration. The reference partition mirror lacks the newer lane at 3a5690d. Keep recipe verification as publication evidence while respecting the decision that the comprehension pilot does not block rollout. See docs/try-it-plan-review-2026-09-13.md.

title: Navigation frame: Learn · Explore · Field guides, seven-lesson rail, position line
description: Masthead becomes Learn · Explore · Field guides (Listen leaves the masthead; the Listen route stays, reached from Start, the dock, and cue rows). Rail lists Start here and the seven lessons only: no subtitles, no book labels, no supplements. Position line 'Lesson n of 7 · book' above every headline; footer keeps Next. AGENTS.md 'the rail and the start page group by book' becomes 'the position line and the start page name the book'. Depends on the lesson 01 epic being judged in use.
acceptance_criteria: All routes unchanged; rail and masthead match the prototype; npm run check green.
notes: Assign to a Claude (Fable) coding peer in its own worktree, with the same brief shape used for Phase A, to compare against the Codex (gpt-6-astra) implementation of fn-5rl. Worktree needs its own Vite port: vite.config.js pins 5173/4173 with strictPort, so run npx vite --port 5174 --strictPort or build and serve dist elsewhere.
close_reason: Reviewer round 4 (13 Sep 2026): the LEARN-headed rail already establishes place; Explore · Listen · Field guides in the masthead works. Leave navigation alone rather than churn it. Reopen only if the pilot says learners are lost.

title: Conventions and iteration record
description: AGENTS.md: replace 'the rail and the start page group by it' guidance only where the drawer changes it (rail stays this round); add the interaction-hierarchy rules (claim primary, hops evidence, drawer closed by default, affordance policy). CONTRIBUTING.md: 'the desktop inspector stays beside the map' becomes a description of the drawer. docs/iteration-6.md: what changed, the two artifact links, verification, not done on purpose (nav frame, Explore page, lessons 02–06).
acceptance_criteria: npm run format passes; the docs describe the shipped behaviour, not the plan.

title: Show the selected claim beside the map so a claim change has a visible result
description: From round five (fn-mjx, second half): on desktop the components a claim changes sit a full viewport below the claims (map begins at y776 on 1440x1000, y1394 on 390x844), so selecting a claim has no visible result until the learner scrolls, and ordinary selection must not scroll. Candidates: a compact selected-claim reminder pinned beside or above the map, a shorter claim area, or an explicitly labelled map-jump action on the claim. Decide after the drawer fixes land; measure the map's document position before and after.
acceptance_criteria: On a fresh lesson at 1440x1000 and 390x844, selecting a claim produces a visible change without scrolling, or a clearly labelled control takes the learner to the map; ordinary selection still does not move the page.

title: Review lesson 03 dependency lanes visually
description: Inspect #spi-boundary on desktop and below 760px. Confirm both compact backend lanes remain in the runtime column, source ownership and sticky behavior are unchanged, all six hops select the intended component in Normal and Cache down, and both detail drawers remain readable.
acceptance_criteria: Desktop and narrow viewport review confirms lane readability, unchanged source ownership behavior, correct six-hop selection, and accessible Redis/Table Storage drawers.

title: Edit lessons 01–03 for direct learner-facing language
description: Editorial review found author/process language in lesson 03 goal (With the drawer closed), a misleading OSDU-versus-Azure question, repeated count framing (Three claims, one map), and branch names introduced before lesson 04 defines them. Lesson 01 should name opendes as the example partition and dev1 as its environment at first use. Keep precise short headlines, concrete commands, and the intentional carry-forward repetition. Suggested replacements are in docs/lessons-01-03-implementation-review-2026-09-13.md.
acceptance_criteria: Goals describe learner understanding, questions name the real code boundary, command flags appear in readable examples, and lesson 03 introduces only enough fork detail to bridge to 04. Recheck the short claim headings and visible map feedback after copy changes. Preserve optional exploration and avoid adding quizzes or progress tracking.
notes: Include the Lesson 01 misconception placement in this editorial pass: profiles are introduced after the required surface, so consider a stack-versus-AKS misconception under the map and keep profile detail with the lifecycle/optional guide.

title: Explore page: #explore chapter on the stack map
description: New chapter entry kind: map, diagram: overview, group: explore, mode: explore. render() skips the lesson frame in explore mode. chapterSteps gives explore ['developer','request']. Every component open, drawer as the explanation surface. Under the map: owner legend and one line of links to the lessons that teach each region. 'Open in Explore' from the stack lessons carrying path and selection. First version covers the stack map only; the boundary, fork, and seam diagrams can join later through a picker.
acceptance_criteria: #explore, #explore/request, #explore?detail=flux resolve; existing chapter-to-renderer and detail-coverage tests pass; no route renamed.
notes: Unblocked from fn-fm9 (navigation frame closed as won't-do in round 4). Still a candidate for Keelson plan-act-evaluate with Copilot; creates a GitHub issue and PR, so needs an explicit go-ahead. Lower priority than lessons 02 and 03.
